newsitem.title: USA: Iowa governor calls for tax cuts in budget.
newsitem.headline: Iowa governor calls for tax cuts in budget.

text.p: Iowa Gov. Terry Branstad on Tuesday proposed $265 million of tax cuts in his $4.3 billion general fund spending plan for fiscal 1998.
In his Condition of the State Message to the legislature, Branstad said the time was right to cut taxes.

"We can cut taxes because we are in a position of financial strength," he said. "We need to cut taxes to make the state more competitive. We must cut taxes to unleash the ingenuity of Iowans to carry this state to a future of unparalleled growth and progress."
The governor said a special task force on economic competitiveness identified both income and property taxes as impediments to attracting news businesses and jobs to the state.
Branstad proposed a 10 percent across-the-board reduction in income tax rates in fiscal 1998, followed by an addition five percent rate drop the following year funded with excess state revenues.

He also proposed $20 million in property tax relief through an increase in the homestead tax credit. The first $200,000 worth of agricultural buildings on family farms would also be exempted from property taxes, under the governor's plan.
Branstad also called for eliminating the inheritance tax for family members and changing formulas and definitions for specific business taxes.

According to the state's budget office, the tax cuts would be accomodated within the $823 million generally accepted accounting principles surplus projected for fiscal 1997, which ends June 30, as well as within revenue projections.
State forecasts show revenue increasing 4.5 percent in fiscal 1998 and 5.5 percent in fiscal years 1999, 2000 and 2001.
A budget summary also indicated that the cuts were sustainable through 2001.
On the school front, Branstad proposed doubling the tuition tax credit for nonpublic schools.
He also recommended the creation of a new department of technology as well as funding for technology programs to make government information and services more accessible to residents.
